slice_results.behavior_summary: At import-time (module-level code), the code requires the 'crypto' module and defines a BloomFilter constructor that generates multiple 4-byte seeds using crypto.randomBytes to initialize internal state buffers, facilitating probabilistic data structure setup with randomized hash seeds.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The analyzed code implements a BloomFilter and CountingFilter data structure using standard cryptographic APIs (crypto.randomBytes) to generate random seeds for hashing. This is a common and legitimate practice in probabilistic data structures to reduce hash collisions and improve accuracy. There is no evidence of monkey-patching, obfuscation, time-based or probabilistic data manipulation, or any attempts to interfere with system or application behavior. The known malicious patterns involve monkey-patching Array.prototype.filter with time-based random data loss or obfuscation of filesystem APIs, none of which are present here. The use of crypto.randomBytes is standard and expected for generating random seeds, not suspicious by itself. Therefore, the code appears benign.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At import-time, the code monkey-patches Array.prototype.filter, intercepts all filter operations, and on Sundays with a 10% probability removes one element from the result, introducing time-based and random data loss.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Introducing random, time-based data loss in a core array method is highly disruptive and can cause subtle, hard-to-debug errors in applications relying on deterministic filtering.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Array.prototype.filter should return a deterministic subset of the array based solely on the filter function. Randomly dropping elements based on the day of the week and probability violates this expectation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use in production. Such behavior might be used in chaos engineering with explicit user consent and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Time-based (day of week) and probabilistic logic to alter results
Randomized removal of elements from filter results
